mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly lower (t-test p > 0.10) when GDPC1 falls by more than 0.5% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate margins, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which is associated with lower earnings expectations and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative correlation (p > 0.10) between INDPRO contraction events and subsequent 60-day S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and accelerating inflation, which increases real interest rates and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and housing starts (HOUST) signals robust household demand and construction activity, which boosts corporate earnings and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS YoY growth and HOUST YoY growth both positive and correlated > 0.6
failure_condition: Correlation between PAYEMS and HOUST growth breaks down or S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the labor force participation rate (implied by stable UNRATE but rising PAYEMS) signals increased labor supply without wage inflation, which supports corporate profit margins and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE stable (±0.1pp) while PAYEMS increases >0.3% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when UNRATE is stable and PAYEMS increases by >0.3%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 5-year average, combined with a flat or declining GDPC1, signals a shift from consumption to savings, which typically precedes a consumer spending slowdown and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 5-year average and GDPC1 flat or declining for 2 months
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (p > 0.10) between the RSAFS/GDPC1 regime and subsequent 60-day S&P 500 returns.
